question.prompt: Let \(v,\) \(w,\) \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) be the degree measures of the five angles of a pentagon. Suppose \(v\lt w\lt x\lt y\lt z\) and \(v,\) \(w,\) \(x,\) \(y,\) \(z\) form an arithmetic sequence. Find the value of \(x.\)

solutions.explanation:
The common difference need not be found, because terms equally far from the middle have opposite deviations from it. Let \(d>0\) be the common difference. Then
\[
v=x-2d,\quad w=x-d,\quad y=x+d,\quad z=x+2d,
\]
so \(v+z=2x\) and \(w+y=2x\).

A pentagon's interior angles sum to \((5-2)\cdot180=540\) degrees. Consequently
\[
(v+z)+(w+y)+x=5x=540.
\]
Thus \(x=\boxed{108}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Pair angles around the middle term
